```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Everything in this article runs on the hard dependencies. Messages and
# warnings are shown, since they are what the article is about; the log lines
# reach the document as messages while knitr runs.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo     = TRUE,
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment  = "#>",
  message  = TRUE,
  warning  = TRUE
)
```

This article lists the messages you are most likely to meet, what each means
and what to do about it. It then covers large layers and long runs: the work
limits, parallel folds, the two caches and the log.
`?"spatialkit-conditions"` lists every warning and error class the package
raises, with the fields a handler can read.

Each message below is quoted as R prints it, up to the point where it starts
to vary. Angle brackets stand for the names and counts that differ from call
to call.

## A layer for the examples

Two examples below run on a simulated layer: 300 points over a 20 km square
in UTM zone 32N, whose unit is the metre.

```{r layer}
library(sf)
library(spatialkit)

set.seed(1)
n   <- 300
pts <- st_as_sf(data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(n, 0, 20000),
                           y = 5e6 + runif(n, 0, 20000)),
                coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632)
pts$w <- rnorm(n)
pts$z <- 2 * pts$w + rnorm(n)
st_crs(pts)$units_gdal
```

## Messages you are likely to meet

### Preparing the data

``build_tessellation(): `boundary` is required for hex/square grids.``
:   A hex or square grid has no extent of its own. Pass `boundary =` a
    polygon of the study area: `st_union()` of your source polygons is one
    way to get it, and `clip_target_for()` builds the bounding box of the
    points. Voronoi cells and `"triangles"` do not need a boundary, since
    they take their extent from the points, or from `cover` when the points
    are seeds.

`prep_model_data(): missing required column(s): <names>`
:   A name in `response_var` or `predictor_vars` is not a column of the
    data. The usual causes are a typo, a difference in case, or a column that
    `read.csv()` renamed under `check.names = TRUE` (`pop density` becomes
    `pop.density`). Check `names(data_sf)`. The geometry column is not a
    predictor.

`prep_model_data(): column name(s) '<names>' are not syntactically valid R names`
:   Every backend builds a formula from the column names, and a name such as
    `B5-B4` or `band 4` does not survive that. Rename the columns before
    fitting, for example with `names(x) <- make.names(names(x))`.

`prep_model_data(): response '<name>' is also listed in 'predictor_vars'.`
:   A model cannot use its own response as a predictor, and none of the
    backends would stop it, so `prep_model_data()` refuses the call before
    any fit. Drop the response from `predictor_vars`.

### Fitting a model

`fit_rf_model(): response '<name>' is not numeric.`
:   The random forest and GWR backends fit a regression, so they refuse a
    factor or character response. The GWR message starts
    `fit_gwr_model(): response '<name>' is not numeric (it is <class>).`
    A number read from a file as text needs `as.numeric()` first; check for
    a thousands separator or an `"NA"` string if that gives `NA`s.
    `fit_gwr_model()` also refuses a response with two whole-number values,
    and names `GWmodel::ggwr.basic()` for it. `fit_bayesian_spatial_model()`
    takes a factor or character response under `brms::categorical()` or an
    ordinal family, and refuses it under any other family with a message
    that starts `fit_bayesian_spatial_model(): response '<name>' is <class>,
    not numeric`.

``fit_rf_model(): `num.trees` is already set by this function and cannot be passed through `...` as well``
:   ranger's own spelling of an argument that `fit_rf_model()` sets would
    reach `ranger::ranger()` twice. Use the wrapper's spelling, which the
    message names, and it passes the value on: `num_trees`,
    `min_node_size`, `num_threads` or `sample_fraction`. `cv_rf()` and
    `compare_models_cv(rf_args = )` pass their arguments to
    `fit_rf_model()`, so the same rule applies there.

### Units and distances

Distances, bandwidths and block sizes are in the units of the CRS a function
works in. When one looks absurd, check that unit first with
`st_crs(x)$units_gdal`. A block size of 1,000 meant in metres is about
305 m on a layer in US survey feet, and a layer in lon/lat is moved into a
projected CRS that `ensure_projected()` chooses, whose unit is the metre.
`?"spatialkit-geometry"` gives the rules, and `vignette("getting-started")`
shows them on a real layer.

`make_folds(block_kfold): the requested grid is <nx> x <ny> = <n> cells, above the 1,000,000 this function will build.`
:   A `block_size` in the wrong unit asks for a grid far finer than meant.
    The message gives the extent and the CRS unit to compare it with:

    ```{r block-units}
    # A block size of 10, meant in kilometres, on a layer in metres.
    # The message is wrapped to fit the page.
    tryCatch(
      make_folds(pts, k = 5, method = "block_kfold", block_size = 10),
      error = function(e) writeLines(strwrap(conditionMessage(e), 76))
    )
    ```

    `predict_surface()` refuses a grid of more than 5,000,000 cells for the
    same reason, and "Large layers" below lists the other limits.

### Cross-validation

`cv_*(): all folds failed (all <n> folds failed to produce predictions); cross-validation results contain no predictions.`
:   The call returns with this warning, `$overall` all `NA` and
    `n_pred = 0`, and the log line of each fold names its cause. A missing
    backend is one cause: `cv_bayes()` without brms fails every fold this
    way, while `cv_rf()` and `cv_gwr()` stop at once when ranger or sp is
    missing. A fit that stops on one fold's training rows fails that fold
    the same way. Here the learner stops on every fold:

    ```{r all-failed}
    cv <- cv_spatial(pts, "z", "w", k = 5,
                     fit_fn = function(train) stop("the backend is not installed"))
    c(attempted = cv$n_folds_attempted, succeeded = cv$n_folds_succeeded)
    cv$overall
    ```

``cv_*(): <k> of <n> fold(s) failed (<causes>), so `overall` pools the other folds only``
:   Some folds failed and the rest were scored. `$overall` then pools the
    folds that ran, and covers fewer rows than the data hold; `fold_status`
    gives the cause of each failure. Every `cv_*()` result records
    `n_folds_attempted` and `n_folds_succeeded`, so compare the two before
    you read `$overall`, on runs that look fine as well.

`compare_models_cv(): no recognised model requested.`
:   None of the names in `models` is `"GWR"`, `"Bayesian"` or `"RF"`, which
    are matched exactly, case included. The warning `ignoring unknown
    model(s)` printed with the error names the ones it ignored.

`compare_models_cv(): no viable models.`
:   At least one name was recognised, but no recognised backend is
    installed. Each prints `dropping <name> (package/function unavailable)`
    before the error, and any name not recognised is named in a warning.
    Install the backend, or ask for one you have.

### Autocorrelation and resolution

`estimate_sac_range()` returned `NA`
:   The range was not identified, so none is reported.
    `attr(x, "rejected_reason")` says why, and `?estimate_sac_range` lists
    the reasons. When the variogram was computed, `plot()` on the result
    (`?plot.sac_range`) draws it, so you can see why the range was
    refused. An `NA` returned before the variogram was computed (gstat
    missing, or fewer than 30 points or locations, for example) carries the
    reason alone.
    `vignette("spatial-cross-validation")` covers choosing a block size.

`determine_optimal_levels(): the model-aware criteria score only the elbow's neighbourhood, k = <a> to <b>, and carry no information at nine cells or fewer`
:   A logged warning. Every candidate around the elbow has nine cells or
    fewer, where Moran's I carries no information, so the call falls back to
    the geometric ranking. On points with no cluster structure, under
    `on_no_elbow = "warn"`, the elbow sits near `sqrt(max_levels)`, and the
    neighbourhood reaches ten cells from about `max_levels = 40`. At the
    default, `on_no_elbow = "na"`, such points return `NA` with a warning of
    class `spatialkit_no_elbow` before any neighbourhood is scored. A line
    logged before the k-means sweep says the same when the ladder itself
    ends at nine cells or fewer.
    `resolution_profile()` scores Moran's z at every level of its ladder;
    see `vignette("resolution")`.

`determine_optimal_levels(): Moran's I could not be computed at any k from <a> to <b> in the elbow's neighbourhood`
:   A logged warning. The neighbourhood reaches past nine cells, but too few
    cells hold a row with a response and every predictor, the regression of
    the cell means on the predictors is singular (a predictor constant or
    collinear across cells), or the cell means differ by rounding alone.
    Check for missing values first. Under `criterion = "morans_i"` the call
    then falls back to the geometric ranking; under `"combined"` it ranks
    the counts as usual, with `moran_i` and `moran_z` `NA` in the
    diagnostics.

### Checking a fit

`n = <n> requires FNN for k-NN weights, and Matrix to hold them sparsely`
:   `residual_morans_i()` on more than 5,000 observations needs FNN to find
    the neighbours and Matrix to store the weights; without them it would
    allocate a dense n by n matrix, so it stops instead. FNN installs with
    spatialkit, so the missing one is usually Matrix:
    `install.packages("Matrix")`. The message names the one it could not
    load.

## Large layers

Most steps take time and memory that grow with the rows or the cells. The
table lists where a function stops, subsamples or leaves a column out on a
large layer. A limit given as an argument is that argument's default.

| function | limit | at the limit | to change it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `make_folds(method = "block_kfold")`, and the `cv_*()` functions that build blocks | a grid of 1,000,000 blocks | error naming the extent and the CRS unit | a larger `block_size` in the CRS unit, fewer `block_nx` and `block_ny`, or a smaller `block_multiplier` |
| `cv_block_size_sweep()` | a grid of 1,000,000 blocks at a size | error for the sizes you pass; a size on the default ladder is dropped, with a log line | larger `block_sizes` |
| `make_folds(method = "nndm")` | 5,000 rows | error | `method = "knndm"`, which has no row limit, or `"block_kfold"` |
| `predict_surface()` | 5,000,000 grid cells | error | a larger `cell_size` or a smaller `n_cells`; `chunk_size`, 5,000 rows, sets the rows per prediction call |
| `create_grid_polygons()`, and `build_tessellation()` for hex and square cells | `max_cells`, 1,000,000 cells, estimated from the bounding box | error | a larger `cellsize`; `create_grid_polygons(max_cells = )` raises the limit, which `build_tessellation()` keeps at its default |
| `residual_morans_i()` | 5,000 observations without FNN and Matrix; 20,000,000 weights (`k` times the observations) | error | install Matrix; a smaller `k` |
| `resolution_profile()` | a level with more than 5,000 cells holding a scored row, without FNN and Matrix | `moran_i` and `moran_z` `NA` at that level, with a warning of class `spatialkit_moran_skipped` | install Matrix |
| `resolution_profile()` on a ladder of sizes, the default | `spatialkit.fit_work_max`, 1e10 point-to-centre comparisons | error of class `spatialkit_work_limit` before any fit | fewer starts, a coarser `obs_per_cell`, random starts of the density kind, or a higher limit |
| searches made without FNN in `resolution_profile()`, `cell_values_at()`, `summarize_by_cell()` and `select_resolution()` | `spatialkit.exact_pairs_max`, 2e9 pairs | by function: an error, `NA` pooled columns with a warning, or the subsample's centres with a log line | reinstall FNN, or a higher limit |
| `estimate_sac_range()` | `n_max`, 5,000 rows | a seeded random subsample, counted in the attributes `n_used` and `n_subsampled` | `n_max`, or `Inf` for no limit |
| `area_of_applicability()` | `normalizer_max_n`, 5,000 training rows | the mean pairwise distance is taken on a subsample | `normalizer_max_n` |
| `summarize_by_cell(deff = "variogram")` | `deff_max_n`, 500 points in a cell | the cell's correlation matrix is built on a seeded subsample of its points | `deff_max_n` |
| `determine_optimal_levels()`, and `resolution_profile()` on a ladder of counts | `sample_n`, 1,500 points | the k-means fits run on a subsample | `sample_n` |
| `fit_bayesian_spatial_model(gp_resolution = )` | 50 basis functions per dimension, 2,500 in all | error giving the basis the range needs | a longer `gp_resolution`; the cost grows with the square of `gp_k` |

`?"spatialkit-options"` describes the two options and what each step does
above its limit.

## Parallel folds

`cv_rf()`, `cv_bayes()` and `cv_spatial()` take `parallel`. `TRUE` uses the
physical cores less one, or `getOption("mc.cores")` when that is lower, and a
whole number above 1 uses that many workers, up to the cores the machine has.
The folds then run in forked workers through `parallel::mclapply()` on macOS
and Linux. On Windows the call runs them one after another, with a message.
`cv_gwr()` takes the argument and runs its folds in turn, with a warning
when more than one worker is asked for. Parallel folds help most in
`cv_bayes()`, where every fold compiles and samples a Stan model.

```{r parallel, eval=FALSE}
cv <- cv_rf(pts, "z", "w", k = 5, parallel = 4L)       # four workers
cv <- cv_bayes(pts, "z", "w", k = 5, parallel = TRUE)  # detects the cores
```

The result depends on `seed` and the fold index alone. The call draws one
seed per fold in the parent process, so `parallel = TRUE` returns what
`parallel = FALSE` returns. With `seed = NULL` the per-fold seeds come from
the session's random stream, and `set.seed()` before the call makes both
runs reproducible.

## Caches

The package keeps two results in the session so that it does not compute
them twice.

`create_grid_polygons_cached()` keeps each grid it builds, keyed on the
boundary's geometry and CRS, the cell count and the other arguments, and
returns the kept grid when the same call comes again. It holds 50 grids
(`max_entries`) and drops the oldest first; `clear_grid_cache()` empties it.
Its grids pass through `ensure_stable_poly_id()`, which reorders and
renumbers the cells, so the same cell can carry a different `poly_id` from
`create_grid_polygons()`. Use one of the two builders throughout an
analysis: a summary keyed on IDs from one and joined to the geometry of the
other can draw the values on the wrong cells.

`fitted()` on a Bayesian GP fit (`?fitted.bayesian_fit`) keeps the
posterior expectations it computes, in an environment the fit carries,
because `summary()` (`?summary.spatial_fit`), `residuals()`
(`?residuals.bayesian_fit`), `model_metrics()` and `compare_models()` each
call it. `clear_fitted_cache(fit)` drops them. You need it only after
editing the `brmsfit` engine in place; a change to `data_sf`, or a refit,
invalidates the entry on its own.

## The log

The package keeps a log through `logger`, apart from R's warnings. Lines at
the INFO level and above go to
`file.path(tempdir(), "spatialkit_model_log.log")`, a file that lasts as long
as the R session, and lines at WARN and above are also printed to the
console. The log has its own `"spatialkit"` namespace: it leaves your global
`logger` configuration alone, and a global configuration set before the
package loads does not carry over into it.

The last line of the file is the warning the failed cross-validation above
ended on:

```{r log-file}
log_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "spatialkit_model_log.log")
# The line is wrapped to fit the page.
writeLines(strwrap(tail(readLines(log_file), 1), 76))
```

`spatialkit_quiet()` turns the console echo off and returns the threshold
that was in force, which puts it back:

```{r quiet}
old <- spatialkit_quiet()
spatialkit_quiet(old)
```

The file and the console are two `logger` appenders, index 1 and index 2.
`logger::log_appender()` and `logger::log_threshold()` change index 1, the
file, unless you name index 2:

```{r appender, eval=FALSE}
logger::log_appender(logger::appender_file("my_analysis.log"),
                     namespace = "spatialkit", index = 2)
logger::log_threshold(logger::FATAL, namespace = "spatialkit", index = 2)
```

A log line is not an R condition: `tryCatch(warning = )` does not catch it
and `suppressWarnings()` does not silence it. "Warnings and log lines" in
`?"spatialkit-conditions"` says how the help pages tell the two apart.

knitr does not capture what is written to the console's error stream, so
while a document is knitted (R Markdown, Quarto, pkgdown) each console line
is also sent as an R message, as the examples above show. A line the package
also raises as an R warning is not repeated, and the chunk option
`message = FALSE` keeps the rest out of the document.
